title: lone survivor: the director's cut
text: ...Eh. I expected a scary experience. A chilling and down right creepy horror game with an interesting story to the likes of the actual Silent Hill games...I got an "Eh" title that tries to do that with muddy graphics and some form of a narrative, but fails to captivate me enough to actually care. Lone Survivor is the 2D, pixelated SIlent Hill, that just isn't. Sure, the monsters creep you out at first, mostly due to the noise they produce then the stickman figure they happen to look like. But they just tend to be more of an annoying blockade in the hallway than something you should fear. This game also brings up some annoying mechanics like an invisible sleeping and eating meter. Cause God knows we need that much "realism" to a game so that people get so "immersed" in it! It's not at all an annoying and unnecesary mechanic, especially when the character ♥♥♥♥♥es and moans about it every 5 minutes. This game also brings back the clunky aiming mechanics of the old Resident Evil. It kinda works for it since it's used in a 2D setting. Though you'll mostly want to avoid confrontation since the enemies  tend to be really bullet absorbent. Which is a plus considering it's a survival horror game. As for the story...I'll be honest, I lost interest in this game after getting to the basement. And I really just did not care what was going on in the appartment. Who that lady in the cage was. If the monsters were actually people and the protagonist was just delusional this whole time. I just didn't give a damn. Why didn't I give a damn. The narrative felt a bit lifeless. I didn't feel like I should actually care what was going on in this world. The fact that most of dialouge amounts to the damn hunger/sleeping meter prompts whenever the protag feels hungry and/or tired may have added to that. Pros: -It's, kind of an interesting take on a Horror game. (Though I wasn't impressed.) -Some of the puzzles were actually kinda clever, like luring a monster to another room by placing meat near it. -You can kinda mix and match items to make new ones, sorta. (From what I experienced, it was mostly to cook food.) Cons: -Hunger and Sleep meter...oh joy. -Muddy pixel graphics (The filter made it seem nice, but it really just adds to it.) -I didn't care for the story or mystery of the game. (Which is a big con considering that's an important motivator to play these types of games.) In short: If you're interested in a 2D, sidescrolling horror game. Try something else. You don't wanna take my word on it and wanna jump into the game anyway? It's your money. Do with it what wish. I recommend you to get it on sale.

title: luftrausers
text: No. Just no. While I appreciate the concept, this is all it is - a concept. You will easily unlock 99% of the content within 3h (or even less) of playing the exact same content. So what's left? missions. I realize that this is an early project of Vlambeer, so I'm writing this review for any future dev who might possibly read this and won't repeat the obnoxious bad decisions that were made here: 1. NO ♥♥♥♥ING RETRY BUTTON!!! In a game that promotes multiple playthroughs in one sitting, you'd imagine this would be mandatory. 2. No consistent way of keeping up your combo multiplier by dealing with inconsistent spawn of large vs small enemies. If the game decides to spawn a bunch of battleships, then expect NOTHING ELSE to spawn for a while until you'll deal with them. rip points, better hit that restart but-- 3. Useless parts, for what reason do they exist? We're talking about toothpick missiles with potato "homing" ability. We're talking about "melee" body that can't sustain more than two bullets. A "Gun" engine that begs you to put it out of its misery. Spread shots that probably got spread damage as well. 4. Absurd missions: Every piece of gear got its own related missions, some are fine, some require legit skill. But we don't wanna talk about those, we wanna talk about the ones that straight up require an rng spawn based on probability of an enemy to spawn. The lowest offender is the Blimp "boss", which spawns generally after hitting a certain difficulty level. The greatest offender is a plane type with lower than 1% chance to appear, mind you that just killing it alone is challenging enough, so the general "strat" would be to use a nuke body and suicide when it spawns. The only problem is that this mission can only be done with a randomized body, so you get 1/5 chance to get the desired plane body part with an additional sub 1% chance to get the spawn you need, so in other words - cancer. All of the bs missions revolve around praying to rngesus to get the spawns you need in order to reach your goal. Overall LUFTRAISERS is a decent game plagued with horrible decisions that were made to maintain its replay value. I cannot support these decisions, and therefore will recommend to simply stay away.

text: This will mostly echo other negative reviews but here goes. Luftrausers in itself is a great game. The controls are tight, the action is fun, and the customization is interesting. However, it's insane that what amounts to a flash game that you would find for free on the internet is sold for $10 on Steam. After a couple of hours, this game completely lost its momentum. It started out great, but it's so shallow that it made me angry that I paid $2 for it on sale. The challenges get to the point that they are too hard to have fun. I don't know how to trigger blimp appearances or make submarines show up, but when the challenge involves destroying one of those specific enemies, the frustration becomes unbearable. It ultimately just becomes a repetitious chore, and the fact that there is only one song during gameplay (which starts over every time you start a new game) doesn't help. Luftrausers is the second game I've ever bought that wound up on my "hidden" list in my games library.

title: luftrausers
text: One word review: a-RAUS-ing What can I say about this game that will do it justice? Short answer. Buy. This. Game. Luftrausers is a 2D, bullet hell, combo based dogfighting game which sees you playing as what is essentially a Nazi fighter pilot in not-so-WW2. You customise your "Rauser" with tonns of different parts that have their powers and weaknesses, like an engine that lets you fly underwater, but will receive more damage if you fly too high, or a body that explodes like a nuclear bomb when you die, allowing you to do a last ditch Kamikaze into one of the many enemies wanting to ruin your day. You can customise your weapon system, your body, and your engine. Depending on which parts you pick will affect the soundtrack in drastic ways. Overall, this game is an absolute gem. Any PC can run it, it has a load of replayability, an amazing soundtrack, slick retro visuals and at a fiver, its a bargain. Pick it up and get Rausing.

title: luftrausers
text: Luftrausers is an entertaining if short lived arcade dogfighting game. The core concepts presented in Luftrausers are a strong backbone for what I would hope the next entry would hopefully embellish. I say this becuase Luftrausers has a delightfully simple control scheme, neat retro visuals, hints at a curious larger universe, and has many fun enemies to combat. However, Luftrausers is lacking in some areas. Namely that the store page bills this game as having over 100 missions, but these are not quests or levels or specific scenarios which change base gameplay in any real way. The missions they refer to are more like challenges. The "story" is extremely limited.  Luftrausers only has a survival/score attack gamemode which doubles as the campaign for the couple hours it takes to play through. While playing through the first "missions" and "story" things were hugely entertaining to discover and every new unlock, every new enemy fought, and every slideshow of "story" was good. But, this is a game which does not have a lot of content past about 3 hours of gameplay. After that, you'll pretty much have seen everything and just be trying out plane combos you didn't try yet, or trying to beat your own highscore. Now I DO recommend Luftrausers, but it is a game I wouldn't recommend too highly because I feel it lacks some features I feel would really round out the package and make it basically perfect. First, as you may have guessed, I am bothered by the lack of a story for the single player. The story isn't a large concern of mine, but an expanded universe would be welcome. Second, the score attack/survival mode in this game is basically perfect except for stopping when the boss is destroyed, but I think Luftrausers could actually benefit from different modes, maybe an objective based mode with specific targets, twists on normal gameplay, and possibly even special plane powers not typically used. Third is leaderboards. This game tracks your score locally for each plane, but you have no comparison to anything but your best run. For competetive people, this may not be enough. I think online leaderboards or even traditional arcade local leaderboards with initials are A MUST! Fourth, local multiplayer with friends with frickin' jets with frickin' missles man. Make it happen in a sequel please! Competetive or cooperative, this is a game I really would love to share with people when they come over! All said and done though, Luftrausers is still a unique game which is undeniably fun for a few hours. Playing as a super fast jet with a nuke inside the body and firing homing missles at crowds of smaller enemy planes to the harmonious and legendary Welcome To The Dangerzone by Kenny Loggins is a memory I will cherish forever, and I have Luftrausers to thank for that. I can also thank Luftrausers for allowing me to finally pilot a Bond movie type vehicle which functions as a jet, a battering ram, and a submarine all at once, sinking destroyers by dropping into the ocean, and surfacing like a majestic humpback whale by crashing straight through the prow of the destroyer and thereby blowing it up. 7/10 overall.
